readme_head:
# FinalProject-NFLBettingMethodAnalysis
Final Project for DTSC 2301:
- Alongside my teammates Malamin Drammeh and Joshua Adeleke, we investigated three popular betting methods — moneylines, spreads, and over/under point totals while using the NFL’s 2025 Season Week 10 data.

- We built and tested three machine learning models (Logistic Regression, Decision Tree, and Naive Bayes) to see if any could reliably predict betting outcomes.

- Key takeaway? No single betting method demonstrated consistent profitability. Spread predictions hovered around 50% accuracy, essentially a coin flip. Followed up with moneyline and over/under reaching ~60%, still not enough for a reliable long-term strategy.

- This project was a great exercise in applying data science and machine learning to a real-world domain, and a reminder that even with predictive models, markets are hard to beat.
